scope: Source-owned bounded WLAN TCP/socket and IPv4 reassembly CPU, with network-layer integration owned by vendor_wireless_network

facts: read_network_connection_all accumulates partial receives until the requested size, EOF, or an error
read_network_connection_nonblocking selects receive mode 0x80
create_network_listening_socket creates and binds before listener preparation, publishing failure before returning
configure_network_connection_options distinguishes no-delay, maximum-segment, send-buffer, and receive-buffer options
dispose_network_connection releases attachment records, buffers, address state, and socket-family storage
The retained connection clock converts source ticks at 2500 microseconds per tick
A zero interval disables the duration threshold; otherwise interval times duration is compared with accumulated elapsed time
Socket completion publishes an error before decrementing the acquired socket reference
Peer and local address results are distinct endpoint projections
Socket wait mode uses flag 0x80 and rejects values other than zero and one
consume_network_fragment advances sequence by the consumed byte count
send_network_transport_fragment_end counts SYN and FIN independently in sequence space and emits reset/ack flags 0x14
Completion and retry callbacks retain socket ownership until callback teardown
Discarding an eligible timed-out entry restores the IPv4 header before emitting control kind 11, code 1
Tail trimming releases the remaining packet chain

replacement_contract.allocation: None; socket count, receive/send storage, fragment count, and assembly payload capacity are const-generic caller-selected bounds
replacement_contract.wire_boundary: Validated IPv4 packets enter receive_ipv4; concrete serialized IPv4 TCP/ICMP packets leave through caller-owned output buffers. No retained stock CPU callback is invoked
replacement_contract.clock: TransportTick is wrapping milliseconds; the embedding scheduler converts its physical tick source at the boundary
replacement_contract.socket_identity: SocketHandle includes an allocation generation; clear invalidates handles and wipes live socket buffers
replacement_contract.sequence_seed: Both active and passive opens require caller-supplied TcpSequence; passive child sequences consume and advance the listener seed
replacement_contract.ordered_state: Active/passive and simultaneous-open handshakes, cumulative/partial acknowledgment, sequence wrap, receive-window flow control, duplicate trimming, zero-window probes, retransmit, graceful FIN/ACK, simultaneous close, time-wait, reset, cancel, timeout and handle teardown are implemented in Rust
replacement_contract.retry_policy: One bounded outstanding segment per socket, at most six transmissions with 1/2/4/8/16/32 second delays; 120-second time-wait. This is replacement policy, not a claim that target defaults have those values
replacement_contract.receive_storage: Receive bytes use fixed circular storage; partial acknowledgments advance a transmit slice without shifting remaining payload
replacement_contract.reassembly: Keyed by both IPv4 addresses, protocol and identification; out-of-order fragments, predecessor-preserving/successor-replacing overlap, last-fragment length, finite capacity, malformed ranges, output capacity, expiry and ICMP reassembly timeout are explicit
replacement_contract.integration: The LAN owner must drain expire_ipv4 and poll, route emitted IPv4 packets through Ethernet/ARP, retain emitted frames until physical transmission completes, and call clear on link/address loss
replacement_contract.physical_failures: A packet-return outcome is serialization, not proof of physical transmission; the LAN runtime owns physical send failure publication and teardown

tests.provenance: Synthetic endpoints and payloads constructed by public socket APIs and the existing public UDP encoder; no captured camera traffic or proprietary packet fixtures
written_unrun: Active/passive handshake, stream transfer, acknowledgment and bidirectional EOF across sequence wrap
Simultaneous active open completes and transfers stream bytes
Lost data acknowledgment causes retransmit without duplicate application delivery; cancellation resets the peer
Short output is retryable and checksum corruption publishes no stream data
Retry exhaustion publishes timeout; teardown invalidates stale handles
A lost receive-window update recovers by probe and stream reads cross the circular-buffer boundary
Out-of-order IPv4 fragments reassemble to a valid original UDP datagram
Overlaps preserve the predecessor; wrapping fragment expiry cannot mix datagrams
Expired first fragments produce a valid IPv4 ICMP time-exceeded code-1 packet
tests.verification: No build, test, lint, formatter, SDK, native execution, emulation, or live camera operation was run

qualification_limits: The pinned C files contain declarations rather than definitions for the main TCP transition and IPv4 assembly routines. Assembly and retry facts above come from authenticated X-M1 A32 bytes, not donor code or NONMATCHING bodies
This source increment is not stock-CPU equivalence evidence or runtime acceptance

Retained socket options, timestamp/window-scale/SACK negotiation, urgent-data presentation, adaptive RTT/congestion-control defaults and connection benchmark framing are not exposed as replacement APIs; the concrete stream uses the base TCP wire protocol and a bounded single-segment transmission window
No missing physical target prerequisite is claimed: source-only integration, independent review and execution qualification remain the integration owner's work
